articles.title: Online enabling checksums in PostgreSQL 19
articles.excerpt: Enabling data checksums is strongly recommended to detect corruption originating in the storage or I/O layer, which can silently lead to incorrect query results. Although PostgreSQL performs basic san…
articles.body: Enabling data checksums is strongly recommended to detect corruption originating in the storage or I/O layer, which can silently lead to incorrect query results. Although PostgreSQL performs basic sanity checks on the page header without checksums, it does not cryptographically verify page contents. As a result, many types of silent corruption could go unnoticed and produce inaccurate query outcomes. In PostgreSQL 18, data pages across database clusters include a checksum by default, which is verified each time a page is read from disk and recalculated when written. Since checksums are enabled for all databases in a cluster, this applies broadly. However, if you've upgraded from earlier versions, your databases likely lack checksums.

articles.title: Atlarix Auto: A Free AI Coding Agent That Picks the Model for Each Step
articles.excerpt: Most AI coding tools ask you to make two decisions before you write a line: which model, and whose API key. Atlarix Auto removes both. It is one option in the model picker — the one new installs start…
articles.body: Most AI coding tools ask you to make two decisions before you write a line: which model, and whose API key. Atlarix Auto removes both. It is one option in the model picker — the one new installs start on — and instead of running your whole session on a single model, it chooses a model for each step of the work. On an account with no credit, Auto in the Atlarix desktop app is free. On Atlarix Pro or credit, it is paid and private. What Atlarix Auto is Atlarix is a desktop coding agent: it plans, edits your code, runs commands in a per-OS sandbox, and runs your tests before it calls anything done, with every change waiting for your approval. Auto is the model setting that decides which language model does each piece of that work. You pick Auto and give it a task.

articles.body: O MockServer é como um "dublê" para sistemas que ainda não existem ou estão fora do ar. Quando um programa precisa conversar com outro sistema (tipo um serviço de pagamento ou uma API externa), ele geralmente faz isso pela internet. O MockServer entra no lugar dele e finge ser esse sistem recebe as mesmas perguntas e devolve respostas de mentira, mas realistas, para que o desenvolvedor teste seu programa como se o sistema real estivesse ali. articles.excerpt: I wanted a vector editor that I could open in my browser and just use . No AI generating things for me, No prompts. No "let AI design it." (tbf it's not that cheap also to offer that for free) Just a…
articles.body: I wanted a vector editor that I could open in my browser and just use . No AI generating things for me, No prompts. No "let AI design it." (tbf it's not that cheap also to offer that for free) Just a vector editor. So I built Scissor. Try it: https://scissor.samalstudios.com/ Initially I wanted to call it OpenScissor and make it open source, but hey I don't want Microsft to train their agens on. It has the usual stuff you'd expect, shapes, paths, text, layers, etc; but the main idea is pretty simple: You make the design. I don't use vector graphics software professionally; so , I didn't really want a massive application with hundreds of features that I'd probably never touch Why I built it? It feels like every creative tool is adding AI to everything these days.

articles.excerpt: O Redis é como um bloco de notas na sua mesa, em vez de um arquivo trancado no porão. https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/clients/nodejs/
articles.body: O Redis é como um bloco de notas na sua mesa, em vez de um arquivo trancado no porão. Sistemas normais buscam dados num banco de dados em disco — seguro, mas lento, como descer ao porão toda vez que precisa de algo. O Redis guarda cópias das informações mais usadas direto na memória RAM, que é quase instantânea. Por isso ele funciona como "cache": acelera sites guardando dados temporários, como sessão de login, carrinho de compras ou contadores em tempo real, para o sistema responder num piscar de olhos.
